topStories.headline: Theo Ellington Wins District 10 in a Landslide, Bringing New Leadership to Bayview–Hunters Point
topStories.dek: The Bayview native and community organizer declared victory Tuesday night after capturing roughly two-thirds of ranked-choice votes in a ten-candidate field.
topStories.body:
Theo Ellington declared a decisive victory in the race to become San Francisco's next District 10 supervisor on election night, November 3, closing out a campaign that proved dominant from the first results to the final count. With roughly 67 percent of votes in the ranked-choice final round, Ellington defeated Dion-Jay "DJ" Brookter, who finished second, and a field of eight other candidates.

Ellington was born and raised in Bayview–Hunters Point and has deep roots in the neighborhood he will now represent. He has served on multiple city commissions, led homelessness outreach with the Salvation Army, and worked as director of public affairs for the Golden State Warriors. He also sits on the board of the Ruth Williams Opera House, a performing arts center in the Bayview. He previously ran for the same seat in 2018 at age 29, finishing third with roughly 20 percent of the vote.

The campaign drew record-level outside spending. Crypto billionaire Chris Larsen made a $500,000 donation to a PAC supporting Ellington — described as the largest individual contribution ever made in a San Francisco supervisor race. Ellington also received endorsements from Mayor Daniel Lurie, the San Francisco Democratic Party, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Instagram co-founder Michel Krieger. Mayor Lurie made a surprise appearance at Ellington's election-night party at Mission Rock Resort.

Ellington has long been engaged in the fight over the cleanup of the former Hunters Point Naval Shipyard. He was a plaintiff in a lawsuit against property developers after the cleanup contractor Tetra Tech EC was accused of falsifying radiological soil test results. District 10 covers Bayview–Hunters Point, Visitacion Valley, Potrero Hill, and Candlestick Point. Walton, who endorsed Brookter, has represented the district since 2018 and is termed out.

As of Thursday, November 5, the San Francisco Department of Elections had released a ballot count that included more than 50,000 additional vote-by-mail ballots, with roughly 86,700 ballots still to be counted. All results remain preliminary until the city certifies the election.

topStories.headline: Third Street Gets Its Flowers: 'Bob Day' Planned for Surfside Liquors Owner, New Businesses Stirring
topStories.dek: The Bayview community is celebrating a neighborhood institution while a fresh wave of Third Street storefronts signals a commercial rebound along the corridor.
topStories.body:
Community members in Bayview are organizing "Bob's Day" — a public celebration for Bob Pinkard, the longtime owner of Surfside Liquors on Third Street — set for Friday, November 7. The event has drawn a social-media push from local residents, according to Mission Local's Bayview Buzz column published November 4, with neighbors describing Pinkard as a cornerstone of the Third Street commercial strip.

The same week brings a spotlight on SCRAP SF, the Bayview arts-and-crafts nonprofit that relocated to a nearly 19,000-square-foot space at 141 Industrial Street this past summer. SCRAP is hosting its annual "Scraptacular" fall fundraiser and silent auction on Saturday, November 14 at that location. Early-bird tickets are priced at $75. The event supports SCRAP's mission of keeping art supplies affordable for San Francisco teachers and artists. An online auction component also runs in the days leading up to the event.

The Bayview Buzz also flagged activity at the Bayview/Linda Brooks-Burton Library Branch at 5075 Third Street, which is hosting a Saturday event in its meeting room on November 7. The corridor has seen a string of new business activity in recent months: a D10 Community Pharmacy is planned for 5668 Third St., a bookstore-and-café called Chapter 3 is expected to open at 4512 Third St. before year's end, and a Bayview Oyster Bar is planned at 5114 Third St. — several of them recipients of Storefront Opportunity Grants from the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development.

topStories.headline: Transit Measure Passes, Offering a Lifeline to Muni and BART Riders in Southeast San Francisco
topStories.dek: Voters approved a Regional Transit Measure on November 3 that could stave off service cuts to the bus and rail lines heavily relied upon by Bayview, Visitacion Valley, and Excelsior residents.
topStories.body:
A Regional Transit Measure on the November 3 ballot passed with what early results described as unexpected ease, according to Mission Local election coverage. The measure was designed to rescue BART and Muni from a mounting financial shortfall driven by the expiration of federal pandemic relief funds and rising operating costs. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency had projected a deficit of up to $322 million by fiscal year 2026–2027.

The outcome carries particular significance for neighborhoods in southeast San Francisco. Transit advocacy organization SF Transit Riders has previously documented that the Excelsior District and surrounding neighborhoods have historically been underserved by transit planning and investment. Bayview–Hunters Point and Visitacion Valley are served by the T-Third Muni Metro line, which SFMTA crews have been maintaining under an overnight maintenance program running through November 2026, with work taking place midnight to 5 a.m. a few nights each week along platforms from Evans to Sunnydale stations.

The San Francisco Bay View noted on November 3 that the Regional Transit Measure could determine whether Bay Area public transportation is preserved for the riders who depend on it most — a group that disproportionately includes residents of lower-income neighborhoods in the city's southeastern corner.

moreNews.headline: Chapter 3 Bookstore-Café Headed to Third Street — First Black-Owned Bookstore in Bayview Since Marcus Books
moreNews.body: Vanessa Lee, co-owner of Smoke Soul Kitchen, filed a permit application this past July to open Chapter 3, a bookstore, café, and wine bar, at 4512 Third Street — a storefront that previously housed a MetroPCS. The project is one of nine Bayview businesses awarded Storefront Opportunity Grants this year by the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development, with grants ranging from $50,000 to $100,000. Lee has said she plans to offer weekend brunch and a wine bar in the evenings. When it opens, Chapter 3 will be the first Black-owned bookstore in Bayview since the relocation of Marcus Books.

moreNews.headline: D10 Community Pharmacy Coming to Third Street After Neighborhood's Last Walgreens Closed
moreNews.body: More than a year after the sole Walgreens in Bayview–Hunters Point shuttered — leaving nearly 35,000 residents without a local pharmacy — a replacement is on the way. The D10 Community Pharmacy, also a recipient of a city Storefront Opportunity Grant, is slated to open at 5668 Third Street, the former site of What's the Scoop ice cream shop. The June 2026 Mission Local report noted that some elderly residents had been receiving life-saving medication by courier since the Walgreens at Bayview Plaza closed.

restaurants.name: Old Skool Cafe
restaurants.description: A 1920s jazz-themed supper club and violence-prevention nonprofit employing at-risk youth ages 16–22, serving Southern soul food with live jazz Wed–Sat evenings.

restaurants.name: Gumbo Social
restaurants.description: Build-your-own gumbo, po'boys, and Cajun-Creole small plates from chef-owner Dontaye Ball, one of Bayview's Third Street anchors; reopened August 17 after a planned summer refresh.

restaurants.name: Smoke Soul Kitchen
restaurants.description: Black- and woman-owned brunch counter in the former Auntie April's space serving fried chicken, waffles, shrimp and grits, and house-made biscuits Wed–Sun.

restaurants.name: Frank Grizzly's
restaurants.description: Family-owned taqueria celebrated for birria tacos, duck tacos, and quesabirria, now settled into its own Bayview brick-and-mortar after launching at Anchor Brewing.

restaurants.name: The Old Clam House

restaurants.name: All Good Pizza
restaurants.description: Brick-oven Neapolitan pizzas, organic salads, and paninis served in a 7,000-sq-ft Bayview beer garden using locally sourced, seasonal ingredients.

restaurants.name: Cafe Alma
restaurants.description: Waterfront café in a 5,000-sq-ft India Basin warehouse serving locally sourced breakfast and lunch Tue–Sat, doubling as a community event, workshop, and live-music venue.

restaurants.name: Gratta Wines
restaurants.description: Bayview's own garage winery producing hand-crafted Dry Creek wines since 2006, with a tasting room, wine bar, and Italian specialty market on Third Street.

restaurants.name: Yvonne's Southern Sweets
restaurants.description: Beloved Bayview institution (est. 2002) selling small-batch pecan pralines, red velvet cupcakes, lemon meringue pies, and butter pecan cookies; reopened this fall and celebrates 20 years on Oct. 4.

restaurants.name: Drew's Barbecue
restaurants.description: Tucked-away Visitacion Valley destination widely praised as the best BBQ in San Francisco, serving ribs, chicken, hot links, and sides Thu–Sat.

restaurants.name: La Joya Café
restaurants.description: Visitacion Valley neighborhood staple on Leland Avenue serving fresh chilaquiles, breakfast burritos, handmade tacos, and espresso drinks made to order daily.

restaurants.name: Pho Luen Fat
restaurants.description: Long-running Leland Avenue standby serving Vietnamese pho, ho fun, Chinese BBQ plates, and Cantonese noodles at affordable neighborhood prices.

restaurants.name: Calabria Brothers
restaurants.description: Excelsior Italian deli beloved for enormous, generously stuffed sandwiches and charcuterie at lunch-counter prices.

restaurants.name: Ty Sandwich
restaurants.description: Excelsior go-to for fresh bánh mì packed with quality ingredients and fast, friendly service at very affordable prices.

restaurants.name: Don Chuy's Mexi-Mercado
restaurants.description: Excelsior corner market with a small kitchen turning out carnitas burritos, quesadillas, and enchiladas that regulars rank among the neighborhood's best.

restaurants.name: Pho Golden
restaurants.description: Highly rated Excelsior restaurant for fragrant pho, noodle soups, and Vietnamese comfort dishes at everyday prices.

restaurants.name: Tala Wine
restaurants.description: Boutique Excelsior wine bar founded by Tala Drzewiecki, curating low-intervention natural wines from small French, Spanish, and Italian producers, with snack plates and tea service.

restaurants.name: The Halfway Club
restaurants.description: Midwestern-inspired Crocker-Amazon bar and restaurant with cult-status chili cheese fries, stiff cocktails, and movie nights — a James Beard Best New Bar semifinalist.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Familiar
restaurants.description: Casual Excelsior sit-down restaurant specializing in pupusas, Salvadoran entrées, and Mexican plates in a family-friendly setting.

restaurants.name: Hawaiian Drive Inn

restaurants.name: Super Star Restaurant
